journey_summary: The site has three entry paths, and each should end at a price and then a booked call. (a) Search or AI-answer visitors land on an article or service page. Each of those pages should hand off in this order: the matching service, one plain price sentence that links to /investment, then /contact. Today several articles never mention price (nonprofit-google-ad-grant, not-showing-up-on-google) and some leaf services never link back to their practice. (b) Home visitors pick a door: /for/local-businesses, /for/founders or /for/nonprofits. From there they go to the right practice or service, then /investment, then /contact. That path works, but it is text-only (zero photos on all three client pages), and it keeps detouring to /work, which has no case studies. Home, founders, local-businesses, coaching, marketing and websites all send people there as if it were proof. (c) Tool users get a result and should be routed to the page that fixes their result. Four tools already do this. The Five-Step Check-Up is the site's main secondary CTA, and it only offers /method or /contact. Its result should name the practice for the weakest step. Two conversion leaks matter most. /investment has no project prices for web builds, branding or video production, so the websites and marketing pages promise "quoted per project" and lead nowhere. And /contact ends by sending people away to a tool.

global_patterns: Where to next strip: a static band placed directly above the closing CTA band on every page except /contact, /ticket and /404. It holds 3 cards, each with a title, one line of copy and a link. Card 1 is the logical next page in the journey (article → its service, service → its practice or client page, client page → its first service, practice → /investment). Card 2 is the matching free tool. Card 3 is the price: one sentence with a real number linking to /investment. Rules: never repeat the closing band's target, never link /work, and never use more than 3 cards. The per-page choices are listed in each page's next_steps.

Sticky mobile booking bar (under 768px only): a slim bar at the bottom that reads 'Book a free call →' and links to /contact. It appears after the visitor scrolls past the hero. It hides while the closing band is on screen, and it is never shown on /contact, /ticket or /404. It has no close button, and its height is reserved with body padding-bottom so it never covers footer links.

One-line price on every service, client and article page, placed near the hero or the first H2. Examples: 'Retainers $1,200–$4,800/mo · strategy $3,000 once · websites from $X → see pricing'. These pages currently state no price: /about, /resources, /method, /tools/checkup, /tools/local-visibility, /tools/ai-opportunity-finder, /articles/not-showing-up-on-google, /articles/nonprofit-google-ad-grant.

Project pricing component. /investment gets a 'Project work' table: Websites (marketing site / booking & lead flow / web app), Brand identity & messaging, Video production (brand film / social video package), Photography, GoHighLevel setup, and the first AI automation build. Each row shows 'from $X', a typical timeline and a link to the service page. Carson sets the numbers; never invent them. The same rows appear as short excerpts on /services/websites (web rows), /services/marketing (brand, video, photo rows) and /services/technical (web, CRM, AI rows), each linking to /investment.

Tool result routing. Every tool's result screen ends with one recommended page chosen by the result, plus /contact. Five-Step Check-Up weakest step: Conviction or A sharp offer → /services/strategy; Your people → /services/marketing; The experience → /services/technical; Word of mouth → /services/local-seo. Can Indy Find You? low score → /services/local-seo. Budget Calculator → /investment. 90-Day Plan Starter → /services/strategy. AI Opportunity Finder → /services/ai-automation.

Photo system: real-looking photos of central Indiana life only. Owners at work in trades, restaurants, retail and salons; founders at laptops or whiteboards; nonprofit staff and volunteers; Indianapolis streets and neighborhoods. No handshakes, boardroom poses, robots or glowing-AI imagery. Never caption or alt-text a stock person as a client or team member. Any slot that shows Carson or the team must use Carson's own photography; Unsplash is only a placeholder for environment shots. Treatment: one consistent warm grade, 4px radius, explicit width and height, AVIF/WebP at 200KB or less, loading=lazy below the fold. No grey captions.
Proof honesty: until case studies exist, 'proof' links point to /method (how we work), /about (who we are) or a free tool. Never point them to /work.
